# h3_vm_security_group_attachment (Resource)

Attaches one security group to a VM and leaves the VM's other groups alone (non-exclusive), so different configurations or modules can each add their own group. Destroy detaches only this group; detaching the last group leaves the VM detached (no groups). At most 5 groups per VM. Applied live, without a VM restart. Do not combine with `h3_vm_security_groups` on the same VM. Uses the point attach/detach API of the network service; where it is not deployed yet the provider falls back to read-modify-write of the VM's list (safe within one apply, not against concurrent changes from the console). Import: `<vm_id>/<security_group_id>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The monitoring module adds its own group to a VM it does not own;
# the VM keeps every other group.
resource "h3_vm_security_group_attachment" "node_exporter" {
  vm_id             = h3_vm.web.id
  security_group_id = h3_security_group.node_exporter.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `security_group_id` (String) Security group ID of the VM's project
- `vm_id` (String) VM ID

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<vm_id>/<security_group_id>`

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import h3_vm_security_group_attachment.node_exporter <vm_id>/<security_group_id>
```
